newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Uzbek president opposes Russia's anti-NATO stance.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek president opposes Russia's anti-NATO stance.

text.p: President Islam Karimov of the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan objected on Wednesday to Moscow's attempts to block the eastward expansion of the NATO military alliance.

Speaking at a news conference with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, Karimov said Uzbekistan, which often has had cool relations with Moscow, backed Czech moves to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

"We support efforts of the Czech Republic on integration into European structures and NATO... we think that a situation when somebody would prohibit somebody else from entering something is impossible," Karimov said.
The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are widely seen as leading candidates among former Soviet bloc countries to join the European Union and NATO.
A July summit of NATO members in Madrid is expected to decide on which countries would be invited into an expanded alliance, and when the integration would take place.
Russia is vehemently opposed to extending NATO eastwards, insisting this would threaten its security but has acknowledegd it has no right of veto.
Moscow said last week that it was drawing up its response to any expansion.
"We do not see that NATO should be a threat for the post-soviet region," said Karimov, who is on a three-day visit in the Czech Republic.

Karimov said parliament in Uzbekistan, one of the more powerful central Asian republics since independence at the end of 1991, recently decided not to seek any pact like one recently created between Russia and Belarus.
"The Uzbek parliament ... decided categorically that Uzbekistan would not participate in military-political blocks," he said.
But Karimov added that Uzbekistan was seeking integration into other international groups such as the European Union.
Prime Minister Klaus said that the Czechs respected Uzbekistan's stability among central Asian countries.
"The Czech Republic appreciates that Uzbekistan is politically and economically the most stable country of the Central Asia region," he said.
